claims.text: In Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency the D.C. Circuit upheld NSA's withholding of UFO-related records; certiorari was denied in 1982.
Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA was decided by the D.C. Circuit in November 1981; the Supreme Court denied certiorari on 8 March 1982.

claims.sourceText: CAUS v. NSA, D.C. Circuit (1981); cert. denied (1982)
claims.text: In Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency (Civil Action No. 80-1562), NSA withheld its UFO-related holdings in full and supported the withholding with an in camera affidavit by Eugene F. Yeates, Chief of NSA's Office of Policy; the D.C. Circuit affirmed in 1981 and the Supreme Court denied certiorari in 1982.

edges.label: CAUS was the plaintiff in Civil Action No. 80-1562
edges.note: The organisation brought the case that produced judicial confirmation that NSA holds UFO-related records it will not release.

edges.label: Chief of NSA's Office of Policy; executed the 1980 in camera affidavit
edges.note: The Yeates affidavit is the operative document by which a US intelligence agency established in court that it held UFO material it could not describe publicly.

edges.label: Appeal exhausted, suit filed
edges.note: CAUS v. NSA is the canonical progression from FOIA request to appellate litigation, and the point at which the courts sustained withholding on a classified affidavit.

edges.label: Courtroom outcomes set the witness's risk calculus
edges.note: The dismissal in Cash v. United States and the withholding sustained in CAUS v. NSA together define the practical ceiling on judicial remedies in this field.

b.label: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency (Civil Action No. 80-1562)

edges.label: NSA withheld its UFO holdings in full and won on an in camera affidavit
edges.note: NSA located responsive material, withheld it entirely, and supported the withholding with a classified affidavit by Eugene F. Yeates. The D.C. Circuit affirmed in 1981; certiorari was denied in 1982.

edges.label: NSA holdings and the FOIA wall
edges.note: The records at issue in CAUS v. NSA are held at Fort Meade, and AARO's current director came from the NSA research organisation based there.

edges.label: Exemption 3 and the Glomar posture
edges.note: NSA's statutory withholding, sustained in CAUS v. NSA on the classified Yeates affidavit, is the hardest documented barrier between sensor data and the public record.

b.label: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency (Civil Action No. 80-1562)

edges.label: The affidavit is the instrument by which withholding was sustained
edges.note: The United States has never asserted that the records do not exist. Its sworn position is that they cannot be disclosed.
